20: timeout: 30_000, 21: }, 22: }); 1: # Samba Media Vault & Metadata Downloader 2: 3: **SambaVault** is a cross-platform media metadata manager, downloader, and Samba (SMB) network share synchronization hub for Movies, TV Series, and Music Albums. Built with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Express, and SQLite, it offers seamless network share exploration, automated metadata retrieval, synopses, and robust watch progress tracking. 4: 5: --- 6: 7: ## 🌟 Core Features 8: 9: - **Media Vault Management**: Organize and catalog Movies, TV Series, and Music Albums with rich metadata (ratings, genres, release years, cover artwork, and director/artist info). 10: - **Embedded SQLite Persistence**: Reliable local storage for titles, synopses, custom tags, and episode watch progress. 11: - **Samba (SMB) Share Sync & Mount Hub**: Connect to local or remote SMB network shares, view folder trees, sync media files, and generate native OS mount commands (`mount_smbfs` for macOS, UNC paths for Windows). 12: - **Metadata Downloader**: Search and fetch professional posters, backdrops, synopses, cast lists, and tracklists. 13: - **Fetch All library metadata**: In Web Search & Categorize, open **Missing & Unfetched** and select **Fetch All** to check items missing a synopsis or poster. Items that already have both appear under **Has metadata**, where they can be reviewed or manually matched. Known category folder labels are excluded without removing anything from the library; standalone files with the same names remain eligible. Detected movie-collection folders can receive a collection overview and descriptions for their member films. Existing metadata and local playback information are preserved. A no-match result can also mean providers were unavailable; retry or use manual matching. Stopping or closing the dialog stops the batch after any current save. 14: - **Universe Matcher**: From All Media, open **Universe Matcher** and select **Match library**. It sends cleaned movie and series titles to TMDB, uses movie collections and a small curated cross-media mapping, and leaves uncertain matches for review. Choose a suggested title, or enter a universe name to create or change a virtual group. Manual assignments and removals are kept on subsequent runs. This does not move or delete files; albums are excluded. Results and overrides are stored in the backend data directory. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB. 15: - **Series Watch Progress Tracker**: Track seasons, episodes, and completed watch states across your TV library. 16: - **Cross-Platform Desktop Bundling**: Native Tauri integration for macOS (`.dmg`, `.app`) and Windows (`.msi`, `.exe`) via GitHub Actions. 17: 18: --- 19: 20: ## 🚀 Getting Started (Local Development) 21: 22: ### Prerequisites 23: - Node.js (v18+) 24: - npm 25: 26: ### Installation & Run 27: 1. Clone the repository: 28: ```bash 29: git clone https://github.com/your-username/samba-media-vault.git 30: cd samba-media-vault 31: ``` 32: 33: 2. Install dependencies: 34: ```bash 35: npm install 36: ``` 37: 38: 3. Start the development server (runs Express backend + Vite frontend on port 3000): 39: ```bash 40: npm run dev 41: ``` 42: 43: 4. Open your browser at **`http://localhost:3000`**. 44: 45: ### Persistent data and backups 46: 47: The desktop app stores its library in `~/.media-player/media_vault.sqlite` and its saved vault state in `~/.media-player/vault_state.json`, outside the application bundle. Replacing the app in `/Applications` should not remove these files. The backend is the single database writer; do not run multiple SambaVault backend instances against the same data directory. 48: 49: Large imports are saved in smaller batches. Keep the application open until pending SQLite writes finish; if saving or loading fails, the app displays a warning. Do not delete the database when troubleshooting a missing library. 50: 51: Library scans and imports ignore `.txt` and `.torrent` files, including custom scan extensions. Existing entries for these files are hidden from the library; the files and saved records are not deleted. 52: 53: Close SambaVault before copying these files for backup or restoring them. Keep backups in a separate location; they contain library and potentially network configuration details. API keys and `.env` files are separate and should be protected, not shared. The backend also supports `SAMBA_VAULT_DATA_DIR` as an explicit storage override; changing it selects a different database. 54: 55: ### TMDB setup 56: 57: Obtain a TMDB **API Read Access Token** (not the shorter API key) and enter it under Settings → API keys. The same section supports OMDb and Gemini keys. Saved values take effect immediately, override environment values, and are not displayed again. Removing a saved value restores any environment value. Settings are available only from the computer running the backend. Keys are stored unencrypted in `~/.media-player/api-keys.json`, or in `SAMBA_VAULT_DATA_DIR` when configured, with owner-only file permissions. Protect the file and do not include it in backups or share it. 58: 59: Alternatively, set `TMDB_READ_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the backend environment or in `~/.media-player/.env` (or `.env` inside `SAMBA_VAULT_DATA_DIR`), then restart the backend. `.env.example` is only a template and is not loaded. Existing environment variables and the project `.env` take precedence over the private `.env`; a saved Settings value takes precedence over all of them. The desktop app inherits environment variables from its launcher. Never commit or share tokens. TMDB requires attribution and its own usage terms apply. 60: 61: ### TVMaze and OMDb search 62: 63: The categorizer and Universe Matcher provide an additional search for reviewing TVMaze and OMDb results. TVMaze searches TV series without a key. OMDb searches movies and series and requires your own `OMDB_API_KEY` in Settings or the backend environment as described above. These searches do not automatically change metadata or universe assignments, and neither provider establishes general universe relationships. 64: 65: In **Web Search & Media Categorizer → Missing & Unfetched**, Fetch All displays a per-item diagnostic log with provider outcomes, cleaned lookup titles, returned titles and years, available fields, and reasons a match was rejected. For movies and series it searches TMDB when configured, followed by OMDb and TVMaze or iTunes fallbacks. A matching filename can supply a year, including a bracketed year; a file belonging to a different title is not used as the year for a grouped folder. With a lookup year, TMDB checks that year first and then the following year; if multiple matches have the same title and year and all have popularity scores, it chooses the most popular, which may be incorrect. Other ambiguous matches require selection. Detected movie-collection folders use TMDB's collection search and details endpoints without requiring a local year; the saved synopsis combines the collection overview with descriptions for its member films. If multiple exact collections exist, choose one from the manual-review candidates. TMDB requires the read access token in Settings. Inferred title variants and nearby-year matches can be wrong and are flagged in the log for review; searches exceeding five result pages remain manual-review cases. For albums, MusicBrainz identifies a unique album and artist, then TheAudioDB provides available descriptions and artwork. A single known artist must be present in the album's metadata; unknown artists or ambiguous matches need manual review. Album titles and artist names are sent to both services. Individual audio tracks are excluded; tracks are not deleted or changed. An album must already exist as a library entry to be searched. The log is cleared on the next Fetch All run and contains library titles; review it before sharing. 66: 67: The separate **Fetch franchise overviews** button searches series and movie collections without a saved franchise overview. Series remain eligible even if they already have a synopsis or poster. Collections are skipped if they have a verified metadata match, a non-placeholder synopsis or artwork, a collection overview, or collection films. It preserves existing fields and saves a separate overview shown in media details. Eligible collections use TMDB first; otherwise Wikipedia is checked for an exact franchise or series page with a premise, overview, synopsis, or plot section. Ambiguous results and series pages whose year cannot be verified require selection. If a manually selected Wikipedia article has no such section, its introduction can be saved instead and is labelled as an introduction excerpt. Wikipedia text is attributed with a source link and CC BY-SA 4.0 license link. Titles are sent to the selected providers; Fandom and TV Tropes are not queried. 68: 69: The diagnostic log also shows provider request URLs, HTTP response status and elapsed time, or whether the request timed out or failed. OMDb API keys are redacted; authorization headers are never logged. URLs include search terms and may reveal library titles and artists. 70: 71: Wikipedia requests identify SambaVault and its project URL, and are sent serially. If Wikipedia responds with HTTP 429 or 503, the app pauses further Wikipedia requests for the provider's `Retry-After` period (at least five seconds if unspecified) and displays when to retry. No Wikimedia login is required, and this does not guarantee immunity from rate limits. 72: 73: Subtitle, artwork and metadata sidecar entries and generic download folder labels are excluded from the categorizer, without deleting files or hiding media inside download folders. A folder with multiple distinct direct child files or folders containing videos is treated as a collection; season folders are not. Explicit collection and trilogy labels also trigger collection lookup. Movies without a trusted local year are saved automatically only when TMDB finds one exact title match; the provider year replaces the placeholder. If TMDB returns multiple matches or only title-variant matches, Fetch All lists the candidates for manual selection. Collection folders are resolved as collections rather than as one film, and require a TMDB collection with usable member descriptions. Release tags are cleaned from lookup titles; other movies require a trusted year, with a one-year tolerance only for explicitly flagged ranked TMDB matches. Series without a trusted year can use a unique exact TMDB title or title variant; the provider year replaces the unverified year. Numbered entries are searched as series only with TV path context, including a numbered file within a matching show folder; otherwise they remain movies. OMDb is skipped for non-Latin titles during Fetch All; use manual matching if needed. An OMDb HTTP 401 or 403 indicates that OMDb rejected the key; check your OMDb key and activation in Settings or the backend environment. A TMDB token does not authenticate OMDb. When no result is available and a provider fails, Fetch All reports a failure rather than recording a definitive no-match. Overly numerous provider results are reported separately for manual review and remain unfetched. 74: 75: Fetch All also strips recognized zero-padded collection numbering with a year and optional genre, edition or subtitle labels, and certain release-group, source, file-size and audio encoding tags after a year. Sequel numbers and subtitle words remain part of the title: when a provider uses a different title or word order, use Manual Match rather than relying on an automatic guess. Titles containing years can still need manual review when the year in the title cannot be distinguished safely from release-year or file metadata. 76: 77: Scanned release years retain their origin: a year found in a file or folder name is distinct from the current-year display placeholder. Fetch All sends only a trusted year and uses the matching rules described above. Filename and folder years must still be supported by a stored name, and a year from a collection label is not treated as a single film's release year. Older entries without provenance are trusted only when their original filename or folder name confirms the stored year. These safeguards may leave items unfetched rather than risk applying an incorrect match. 78: 79: Fetch All stops if the metadata backend is unreachable instead of recording offline cache responses as no matches. The packaged desktop app must be rebuilt and restarted after backend changes; its local backend listens on `127.0.0.1:3000`. For development, run `npm run dev`. Once the backend is running, retry Fetch All; it includes incomplete items previously marked no-match. 80: 81: --- 82: 83: ## 📦 Production Build 84: 85: To build the Tauri desktop app with its backend, Node.js runtime, frontend assets, and media tools bundled: 86: ```bash 87: npm run tauri -- build 88: ``` 89: 90: The packaged app starts the local backend automatically and stops it when the app exits. Desktop release builds require FFmpeg and FFprobe on the build machine. `npm run dev` remains the development command and starts the backend alongside Vite. 91: 92: --- 93: 94: ## 🤖 GitHub Actions CI/CD & Automated Release Tags 95: 96: This repository includes an automated GitHub Actions release workflow in `.github/workflows/release.yml` with cross-platform desktop bundling for **macOS** (`.dmg`), **Windows** (`.msi`), and **Linux** (`.deb`, `.AppImage`). 97: 98: ### Release Versioning (`0.0.1` → next push `0.0.2`): 99: - The header displays the version embedded in the running app, not the latest GitHub release. Release builds synchronize this version to the selected release tag; local builds use the version in `src/version.ts`. Click the badge to open version settings. A differing backend version is shown as a mismatch, not as an available update. 100: - **Automated Push Tagging**: Whenever you push code to `main`, GitHub Actions automatically: 101: 1. Inspects the latest release tag in the repository. 102: 2. Bumps the patch version: `0.0.1` on first release, then next push `0.0.2`, `0.0.3`, etc. 103: 3. Tags the commit on GitHub and creates the GitHub Release with the version tag (`0.0.1`, `0.0.2`). 104: 4. Automatically synchronizes `package.json` and `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`. 105: 5. Compiles and uploads native desktop bundles for macOS, Windows, and Linux to the release assets. 106: 107: - **Manual Tag Release**: You can also push custom release tags directly: 108: ```bash 109: git tag 0.0.1 110: git push origin 0.0.1 111: ``` 112: Or using `v` prefix: 113: ```bash 114: git tag v0.0.2 115: git push origin v0.0.2 116: ``` 117: 118: - **Local Version Bump Helpers**: 119: ```bash 120: npm run bump:patch # Increments patch (e.g. 0.0.1 -> 0.0.2) across all files 121: npm run bump:minor # Increments minor (e.g. 0.0.2 -> 0.1.0) 122: npm run bump:major # Increments major (e.g. 0.1.0 -> 1.0.0) 123: npm run version:sync 0.0.3 # Syncs all files to explicit version 124: ``` 125: 126: --- 127: 128: ## 📁 Project Structure 129: 130: - `/src`: Frontend React application (Components, Views, State management, Tailwind CSS styling) 131: - `/server.ts`: Express backend API & SQLite database service 132: - `/src-tauri`: Tauri desktop configuration and Rust native bridge 133: - `/.github/workflows`: CI/CD release pipeline 134: - `/metadata.json`: Application metadata and capabilities1: 1: import express, { Request, Response } from 'express';
